primary_failure_classification.statement: near-homology is the dominant cause of the q<0.01 null-imbalance/FDP failure in this dataset

broader_calibration_classification.statement: near-homology is one important contributor among several to pooled PEP miscalibration

causal_answer: Biologically structured false targets in proteins capable of producing highly native-homologous peptides are a causal reason reversed decoys fail to represent the high-scoring false-target distribution after Percolator rescoring in this dataset.

pep_calibration.interpretation: High-confidence PEP calibration improves strongly; pooled improvement is modest and uncertain.

fdp_calibration.interpretation: FDP calibration improves clearly across the useful q-value range.

training_dose.interpretation: Homology depletion removes training-induced amplification of null imbalance but not the training-associated rise in pooled PEP error.

bin_level_relationship.interpretation: The approximate one-to-one factorization persists; correlation attenuates under intervention-induced range restriction.

remaining_unexplained: positive pooled PEP error after depletion
whole-protein treatment cannot isolate witness peptides from correlated biological composition
next_experiment: Repeat the frozen paired design prospectively on independent biological datasets with equal-opportunity close- and distant-phylogeny entrapment panels at predeclared homology strata.
